question: Should ClawHub change its publishing contract from a uniform MIT-0 policy to accepting and persisting package-declared standard MIT for skills?
rationale: This affects legal terms shown to users, consent language, stored versions, backfills, public API responses, CLI output, and documentation; code review cannot safely decide the intended permanent license policy.

options.title: Sponsor dual-license support
options.body: Approve MIT and MIT-0 as the supported stored licenses, then require a rebase plus fresh publish/import and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Keep uniform MIT-0
options.body: Retain the existing platform-wide MIT-0 policy and close or substantially narrow this PR rather than deriving license terms from uploaded packages.

options.title: Define a narrower policy first
options.body: Pause the PR until maintainers specify whether declared licenses may be displayed, accepted only for imports, or must be restricted to a different package contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor dual-license support
recommendation.body: Approve MIT and MIT-0 as the supported stored licenses, then require a rebase plus fresh publish/import and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They can supply the requested implementation and proof context, although a repository publishing-policy owner must make the final product decision.
